questions.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{v,w\}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ 
And, since the set $\{v,w\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by 

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1}\}$ and $\text{Span}\{{a}_{2}\}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{3\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 1+4\cdot 1}{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}v=\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{3\cdot 2+1\cdot 1+4\cdot 1}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}w=\frac{11}{6}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+\frac{11}{6}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(4[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+11[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ \frac{5}{2} \\ \frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is orthogonal.
questions.worked_solution:
Since the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1}\},$ $\text{Span}\{{a}_{2}\},$ and $\text{Span}\{{a}_{3}\}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{1\cdot (-1)+4\cdot 1+3\cdot 1+1\cdot 1}{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{1}=\frac{7}{4}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{1\cdot 3+4\cdot 1+3\cdot 1+1\cdot 1}{{3}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{11}{12}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{3}}{{a}_{3}\cdot {a}_{3}}{a}_{3}=\frac{1\cdot 0+4\cdot (-2)+3\cdot 1+1\cdot 1}{{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=-\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x \\  & =\frac{7}{4}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+\frac{11}{12}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}(21[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+11[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-8[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ -3 \\ -12\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is orthogonal.
questions.worked_solution:
Since the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1}\},$ $\text{Span}\{{a}_{2}\},$ and $\text{Span}\{{a}_{3}\}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{0\cdot (-1)+(-1)\cdot 0+(-3)\cdot 2+(-12)\cdot (-2)}{(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 4 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{0\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 0+(-3)\cdot 2+(-12)\cdot 1}{{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 0 \\ -4 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{3}}{{a}_{3}\cdot {a}_{3}}{a}_{3}=\frac{0\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 0+(-3)\cdot (-1)+(-12)\cdot (-2)}{{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-2)^{2}}{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ -3 \\ -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 4 \\ -4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 0 \\ -4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ -3 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -3 \\ -12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 6 \\ 14\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{v,w\}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ 
And, since the set $\{v,w\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by 

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1}\}$ and $\text{Span}\{{a}_{2}\}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{10\cdot (-2)+6\cdot 1+14\cdot 3}{(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}}v=2[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{10\cdot 2+6\cdot (-2)+14\cdot 2}{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}}w=3[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -6 \\ 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2 \\ 6\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -6 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 3 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is orthogonal.
questions.worked_solution:
Since the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1}\},$ $\text{Span}\{{a}_{2}\},$ and $\text{Span}\{{a}_{3}\}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{7\cdot 1+3\cdot (-1)+(-1)\cdot 1+4\cdot 0}{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{7\cdot 1+3\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot 0+4\cdot 2}{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}}{a}_{2}=3[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{3}}{{a}_{3}\cdot {a}_{3}}{a}_{3}=\frac{7\cdot (-3)+3\cdot (-1)+(-1)\cdot 2+4\cdot 2}{(-3)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}}{a}_{2}=-[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+3[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+(-1)[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ 0 \\ 6\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 3 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
